name: INA228 85 V 20-bit power monitor
description: Texas Instruments 20-bit current, voltage and power monitor with an I2C interface: measures a 0–85 V bus (195.3125 µV per count) and the voltage across a shunt resistor (±163.84 mV, 312.5 nV per count), and reports current in amperes once its SHUNT_CAL register is set. Runs on 2.7–5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit INA228 I2C 85V, 20-bit High or Low Side Power Monitor (#5832), 8-pin header VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, VBUS, VIN-, VIN+, ALRT plus a 3-pin screw terminal (V-, VBus, V+), 15 mΩ shunt (up to 10 A), I2C address 0x40 (0x41/0x44/0x45 with the A0/A1 jumpers).
eli5: Sits in the wire to a motor, battery or solar panel (up to 85 V) and tells your board very precisely how many volts and amps are flowing.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Logic supply 3–5 V (chip 2.7–5.5 V); use the same voltage as your microcontroller (3.3 V on ESP32/Pico)

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground, shared with the measured circuit's ground

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up on the board)

pins.name: VBUS
pins.description: Bus-voltage sense input, 0–85 V; bridge the back VBUS jumper (high side) or wire it to the supply rail. Never to a GPIO.

pins.name: VIN-
pins.description: Shunt low side: to the load's + lead (high side). Up to 85 V; never to a GPIO. Same net as the terminal's V-.

pins.name: VIN+
pins.description: Shunt high side: from the supply being measured. Up to 85 V; never to a GPIO. Same net as the terminal's V+.

pins.name: ALRT
pins.description: Alert output (open-drain, active low); not needed for basic use

buildNotes: Put the shunt in series with the load: supply + to VIN+ (terminal V+), VIN- (terminal V-) to the load's +, and the measured supply's ground to the same GND as the microcontroller.
VBUS is open by default (low-side use): bridge the VBUS jumper on the back for high-side sensing, or wire VBUS to the supply rail, otherwise the bus voltage reads 0 V.

VIN+, VIN- and VBUS may carry up to 85 V: never connect them to a GPIO. The 15 mΩ shunt reads up to about ±10 A (±163.84 mV); carry the load current through the screw terminal with thick wire, never through breadboard rows or the header pins.
Write SHUNT_CAL (02h) = 13107.2e6 × CURRENT_LSB × 0.015 before reading CURRENT (07h); with CURRENT_LSB = 20 µA that is 3932. Current = CURRENT_LSB × CURRENT.
VBUS (05h) and CURRENT (07h) are 24-bit registers: read 3 bytes, the 20-bit result is in bits 23-4. Bus voltage = VBUS × 195.3125 µV.
MANUFACTURER_ID (3Eh) reads 5449h and DEVICE_ID (3Fh) 228xh: a quick wiring check. Default address 0x40; bridge A0 for 0x41, A1 for 0x44, both for 0x45.

driver.code:
# INA228 85 V, 20-bit current / voltage / power monitor (TI INA228, SLYS021A), MicroPython driver.
# Register pointer byte, then data MSB first. CONFIG, ADC_CONFIG, SHUNT_CAL and the ID registers
# are 16-bit; VSHUNT, VBUS and CURRENT are 24-bit (read 3 bytes) with the 20-bit result in bits 23-4.
#   05h VBUS:    bits 23-4, LSB 195.3125 uV (always positive).
#   07h CURRENT: bits 23-4, two's complement, Current [A] = CURRENT_LSB x CURRENT (datasheet eq. 4),
#                valid once SHUNT_CAL (02h) = 13107.2e6 x CURRENT_LSB x R_SHUNT (eq. 2, ADCRANGE = 0).
#   3Eh MANUFACTURER_ID = 5449h ("TI"), 3Fh DEVICE_ID = 228xh (DIEID 228h + revision).
# Defaults suit the Adafruit INA228 breakout (#5832): 15 milliohm shunt, up to 10 A.
import time

_CONFIG = 0x00
_ADC_CONFIG = 0x01
_SHUNT_CAL = 0x02
_VBUS = 0x05
_CURRENT = 0x07
_MANUFACTURER_ID = 0x3E
_DEVICE_ID = 0x3F

# MODE = Fh (continuous bus, shunt and temperature), VBUSCT = VSHCT = VTCT = 5h (1052 us),
# AVG = 2h (16 samples): a fresh result about every 16 x 3 x 1.05 ms = 50 ms.
_ADC_SETTINGS = 0xFB6A


class INA228:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x40, shunt_ohms=0.015, max_amps=10.0):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if self._read16(_MANUFACTURER_ID) != 0x5449 or (self._read16(_DEVICE_ID) >> 4) != 0x228:
            raise OSError('INA228 not found at 0x%02x: check the wiring' % addr)
        # ADCRANGE = 0 (+-163.84 mV across the shunt). CURRENT_LSB must be at least
        # max_amps / 2^19 (eq. 3); use a round 20 uA for the 10 A default.
        lsb = max_amps / 524288
        self.current_lsb = 20e-6 if lsb <= 20e-6 else lsb
        cal = int(13107.2e6 * self.current_lsb * shunt_ohms + 0.5)
        if not 0 < cal < 0x8000:
            raise ValueError('shunt_ohms / max_amps give SHUNT_CAL out of range')
        self._write16(_CONFIG, 0x8000)  # RST: back to power-on defaults (self-clearing)
        time.sleep_ms(2)
        self._write16(_CONFIG, 0x0000)  # ADCRANGE = 0, no conversion delay
        self._write16(_SHUNT_CAL, cal)
        self._write16(_ADC_CONFIG, _ADC_SETTINGS)
        time.sleep_ms(60)  # wait for the first averaged result

    def _write16(self, reg, v):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([(v >> 8) & 0xFF, v & 0xFF]))

    def _read16(self, reg):
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 2)
        return (d[0] << 8) | d[1]

    def _read20(self, reg):
        """A 24-bit result register: the 20-bit value in bits 23-4."""
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 3)
        return ((d[0] << 16) | (d[1] << 8) | d[2]) >> 4

    def bus_voltage(self):
        """Voltage on VBUS relative to GND, in volts (195.3125 uV per count)."""
        raw = self._read20(_VBUS)
        if raw & 0x80000:  # two's complement field, always positive in practice
            raw -= 0x100000
        return raw * 195.3125e-6

    def current_ma(self):
        """Current from VIN+ to VIN- in mA (negative when it flows the other way)."""
        raw = self._read20(_CURRENT)
        if raw & 0x80000:
            raw -= 0x100000
        return raw * self.current_lsb * 1000

    def power_mw(self):
        """Power delivered to the load in mW (bus voltage x current)."""
        return self.bus_voltage() * self.current_ma()

    def read(self):
        """Return (bus voltage in V, current in mA)."""
        return self.bus_voltage(), self.current_ma()

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from ina228 import INA228

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = INA228(i2c)  # address 0x40, 15 milliohm shunt, 20 uA per count
while True:
    v, i = sensor.read()
    print('V=%.3fV I=%.1fmA' % (v, i))
    time.sleep(1)
